speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; to help me determine the cause, how long has this dizziness been lasting, and does it worsen when you turn your head or change position?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The 3-minute duration of spinning dizziness triggered by changing position (going to bed) in a previously healthy 59-year-old male is classic for BPPV, so I will now request a Dix-Hallpike maneuver and a head CT to rule out posterior circulation stroke given his age and sudden onset. REQUEST TEST: Head_CTI; REQUEST IMAGES: Dix-Hallpike_Manuever_Videos.
